heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) — advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a cinematic dark hero with a layered media collage rather than a simple split layout: place the headline and CTA in a left content block over a subtle grid/mesh, and build the right side as a stacked showcase of one autoplay-muted hero loop plus two preview cards for image generation and video generation. Keep the amber brand accent only for CTA, chip highlights, and key data points. Add soft floating orbs, faint grid lines, and a premium glass panel treatment to make the section feel like an enterprise creative studio. The hero should look high-end, production-ready, and proof-led, with motion preview taking priority over static imagery.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is split and dark, while the trust section becomes a compact logo proof band on a light surface.
Product sections alternate between a preview-led split panel and a deep dark showcase strip to avoid same-pattern adjacency.
Pricing is simplified into a centered comparison-like card set after a dense features block, creating a calmer cadence.
Testimonials use a different visual rhythm from products by shifting to a spotlight carousel/grid treatment.
The final CTA/form block is isolated as a high-contrast conversion moment rather than repeating the earlier storytelling structure.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Images & Videos for Enterprise Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance for premium AI image and video generation. Built for creative teams, marketing leaders, and enterprises needing high-quality multimodal content.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark cinematic base with subtle floating-orb glow and amber edge highlights
sections.designNote: Use a content-first hero that directly answers what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Left side: headline, subheadline, supporting line, and a single solid amber CTA labeled Get started. Right side: premium visual stack with one large video preview and two smaller image thumbnails, styled like a creative studio dashboard. Keep the headline tight and scan-friendly even though the source copy is long. This section should feel dynamic and immediate, matching the ad message and setting the premium production-ready tone.

Place proof early because traffic is warm and the buyer is enterprise-minded. Use 3-6 recognizable logos in a clean static flex-wrap grid; if real logos are unavailable, replace with a metric strip. Keep this section compact and calm, with minimal decoration, so the page transitions from cinematic hero to credibility without losing momentum.

Treat the two product sections as distinct but related pillars rather than a generic SaaS feature grid. First block: Seedream 4.5 in a split, visual-first layout with a preview panel and a short, dense feature list focused on image quality, text rendering, composition, and editing control. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in the opposite visual direction, with a darker showcase panel and motion-oriented callouts for text-to-video, audio-visual sync, lip-sync, and cinematic camera control. Because there are 5+ features across the section set, avoid a flat static card grid; use alternating panels with spotlighted feature groupings instead. Keep the energy premium and editorial, not modular and generic.

Present pricing as a lead-generation decision block rather than a transactional store. Use two centered cards with one slightly emphasized as the recommended next step, but keep the overall structure restrained. Make the pricing feel consultative and enterprise-friendly, especially for the video plan with the starting monthly price. All primary actions on cards must still use the exact CTA text Get started.

Because there are 4+ testimonials, use a carousel-static or spotlight treatment rather than a flat card wall. Prioritize quotes from creative director, video producer, and art director first since they best match the buyer persona. Keep the quote layout airy and polished, with one featured quote and smaller supporting cards or slides. This section should feel like peer validation, not marketing copy.

Use the final conversion moment as a dark, high-contrast lead capture strip with a floating card or simplified form prompt. Keep the message focused on seeing the product in action, not on committing to a purchase. The CTA must be Get started, full-width on mobile, and filled with the accent color at 100% opacity. This is the closing conversion beat, so it should feel decisive and friction-light.

Use this only if needed as a minimal closing trust/footer row, not as a marquee. Prefer static logo-strip styling or a simple horizontal utility row. Keep it understated so it supports the primary conversion path rather than competing with it.

blueprint.designPersonality: High-end creative AI studio for enterprise teams: cinematic but controlled, minimal but not sterile, with strong proof-first hierarchy, rounded premium cards, amber brand accents, and dark visual showcases balanced by clean white content sections.

Keep faces optional and only use them if they appear naturally in the media; do not force human portraits into the hero.

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with a strong product-led headline and concise multimodal value proposition
Prominent logo strip as the main trust layer near the top, since logos are the strongest proof signal for this audience
Human face or real professional usage context in the hero, paired with product UI or output visuals without generating fake-looking imagery
Dedicated image gallery section showcasing Seedream 4.5 outputs and editing capabilities
Dedicated video gallery section showing Seedance 1.5 Pro motion quality, audio-video sync, and cinematic storytelling
Clear feature storytelling for each model with readable stacked content blocks rather than complex nested grids
Strong CTA placement near hero and again after product sections to support demo/quote intent
Testimonial section presented as a slider to keep the page compact and improve scanability
Pricing/quote block positioned as enterprise inquiry-oriented, not ecommerce-style checkout
Final conversion block with a focused request-demo or get-quote action
avoidPatterns: Do not use a testimonial grid; use a slider instead
Do not overload the hero with long copy or oversized supporting text
Do not crop or darken hero visuals in a way that hides the face or product context
Do not introduce extra lead magnets or distracting secondary conversion paths
Do not use grid-inside-grid layouts for feature sections
Do not rely on generic abstract visuals when real output examples and human context are available
Do not add mismatched content beyond the provided product scope
Do not make the layout overly decorative or glassy; keep it functional and premium
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a high-intent, enterprise-oriented lead-generation landing page for two advanced ByteDance generative models, so the structure should prioritize fast understanding, proof, and demo conversion. Because the audience is professional and decision-oriented, the story should be product-led with strong visual evidence rather than editorial or pain-heavy storytelling. The strongest trust cue is logos, so brand proof should dominate above testimonials and be placed early. The dark theme supports a premium AI positioning, while immersive hero treatment with a human face and product/output visuals better fits professional creative tools. Since the content includes both image and video generation, separate gallery moments are important to demonstrate capability clearly. Feature sections should remain readable and linear, and testimonials should be in a slider to avoid clutter while preserving credibility. Overall, the page should feel high-end, efficient, and conversion-focused, with one primary action: request a demo or get a quote.
